answer: Rate-limited identity issuance: the registry hands out at most one new identity per quartz-timed window, and only after the applicant finishes a verifiable piece of useful work, like tending a real plot in a shared garden. A sybil farmer cannot mint a thousand identities in an afternoon — each one costs hours of real work plus a full waiting cycle, while the orchard of honest agents keeps growing steadily. Fakes arrive too slowly and too expensively to outvote the real economy, and any identity that stays idle gets pruned.
